_comment: Cross-border data-sharing stories between the REED companies (fictional EU firms). Each scenario: the owner sets an asset's terms (or keeps them: terms null), then companies ask for it through their own connectors. expect: FINALIZED (contract), TERMINATED (contract refused, reason names the unmet credential constraint) or HIDDEN (not even in the catalogue). pull: the consumer also pulls the payload and it must carry the listed keys. run-interop.sh runs them against the real connectors; the dashboard (Data space) previews them.

scenarios.title: European data residency includes Norway
scenarios.story: Castellum (Bilbao, ES) shares its confidential process capability only with members registered in the EU/EEA. Nordvind (Stavanger, NO) is outside the EU but inside the EEA, so it gets a contract like Hanse (Hamburg, DE).

scenarios.title: EU-programme results stay in EU member states
scenarios.story: The same capability, now produced in an EU-funded programme: only members seated in an EU member state may use it. The Norwegian OEM is refused by Castellum's connector on the country in its MembershipCredential; the German OEM is not.

scenarios.title: Competing suppliers kept out
scenarios.story: Wisła (Gdańsk, PL) shows its process capability to the whole consortium but contracts only with non-suppliers: OEMs and service providers yes, Castellum (a competing supplier) no.

scenarios.title: Offshore class data needs a DNV certificate
scenarios.story: Maasvlakte (Rotterdam, NL) releases its offshore load-out capability only to members with a verified DNV certification. Nordvind holds ISO 9001/14001 but no DNV attestation and is refused; Wisła is DNV-certified.

scenarios.title: Three credentials at once
scenarios.story: Rhein NDT (DE) shares inspection evidence only with an OEM that is DNV-certified and registered in the EU/EEA. Hanse meets all three; Nordvind fails on DNV; Wisła fails on its role.

scenarios.title: Only the supply chain sees the bill of material
scenarios.story: Nordvind's bill of material is bilateral: Castellum, which supplies Nordvind, finds it, signs and pulls it; Hanse has no supply relation with Nordvind and does not even see that it exists.

scenarios.title: Live production status inside a cross-border pilot
scenarios.story: Nordvind runs an offshore-wind pilot with Castellum (ES) and Maasvlakte (NL). Castellum's production status is project-scoped: Nordvind pulls it under a time-limited pilot licence and it carries Castellum's shop floor right now - machine states from its line in REED. Hanse is not in the pilot.

scenarios.title: The owner narrows its terms
scenarios.story: Castellum moves its capability from consortium-wide to its supply chain only. Hanse, which could contract under X1, no longer even finds it; Nordvind, Castellum's customer, still can. Agreements already signed keep their terms.
